stem: A child has a fixed split second heart sound on examination. Which mechanism best explains this classic finding in atrial septal defect?

options.text: Delayed pulmonary valve closure from increased right-sided flow

explanation: A fixed split second heart sound in atrial septal defect reflects delayed pulmonary valve closure due to increased right-sided volume and a relatively constant left-to-right atrial shunt across respiration.
